\chapter{Ese --- Pointing at What Is by You}
\label{ch:ese}
\hlchaptermodality{222}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can point at something on my listener's side.}

I can point at something on my listener's side.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ese]{ese — pointing at what is by you}

\label{lesson:ES-C59-ese}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Este libro} is the one in my hand.

Remember where \emph{este} came from: it used to point at \textbf{you}. So when it moved to me, something had to take over the job it left behind.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{ese libro} — \emph{that book}, the one near \textbf{you}.

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{\textbf{ese}} \emph{libro} & that book, by you \\
\emph{\textbf{esa}} \emph{casa} & that house, by you \\
\emph{\textbf{esos}} \emph{libros} & those books \\
\emph{\textbf{esas}} \emph{casas} & those houses \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

The word that stepped in was Latin \emph{\textbf{ipse}}, which meant \textbf{self} — the same \emph{ipse} in the Latin phrase \emph{ipso facto}, \textquotedblleft{}by the fact itself\textquotedblright{}.

You can feel how it got the job. \emph{That very one}, \emph{that one itself} — an emphasiser that keeps insisting on a particular thing eventually stops emphasising and simply \textbf{points}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{culture}
So the difference between \emph{este} and \emph{ese} is not distance in metres. It is \textbf{whose side the thing is on}.

\begin{quote}
\emph{Este libro} — mine, here. \emph{Ese libro} — yours, there.
\end{quote}

Two people sitting at one small table will still say \emph{este} and \emph{ese} about books a hand's width apart, because the question was never how far away the book is. It is which of us it belongs to in this moment.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{este libro}, then \emph{ese libro}
  \item \emph{esa casa}, \emph{esos libros}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Whose side is \emph{ese} on? (\textbf{Yours} — the listener's.)

And what filled the slot when \emph{iste} moved closer? (\emph{\textbf{Ipse}}, the word for \emph{self}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
